name: Revenue recognition
description: ASC 606, schedules, adjustments and period close.
takeaways: Rules decide how each product is recognised; criteria use equals only, joined by AND
Month end: run the job, review drafts, transfer

cards.title: Five steps
cards.body: ASC 606 and IFRS 15: identify the contract, identify performance obligations, determine the price, allocate it, recognize revenue. Zenskar identifies obligations from the products and features in each phase.
cards.example: A subscription plus onboarding gives two obligations.

cards.title: Over time or at a point
cards.body: Subscriptions and managed services are recognized over time; deliveries and milestones at a point in time.
cards.example: A delivery is recognized on delivery.

cards.title: Distribution methods
cards.body: Over-time obligations get a baseline schedule: straight-line, usage-based (tied to consumption) or entitlement-based (credits, milestones, features).
cards.example: $12,000 per year straight-line is $1,000 per month.

cards.title: Adjustment methods
cards.body: When reality changes, a revised schedule is built by front-load (next open period, required for material changes above 5%), straight-line over remaining periods, or back-load (final period).
cards.example: A 10% scope increase is front-loaded.

cards.title: Monitoring and audit
cards.body: Zenskar watches for scope changes, usage variance, variable consideration and FX. Each adjustment keeps its rationale, approval workflow and audit trail.
cards.example: Usage overshoots forecast, so the schedule is revised.

cards.title: Ledger objects
cards.body: Chart of accounts, accounts, journal entries and lines, balance sheet and income statement.
cards.example: A journal entry per recognized amount.

cards.title: Period close
cards.body: Validate period close returns a checklist without closing. Closing then locks the period: no transactions inside it can be modified.
cards.example: Validate March, fix gaps, then close.

cards.title: Revenue rule library
cards.body: Where you define how each product is recognised: name, revenue account, satisfaction type, distribution method and criteria. Find it under Accounting, then Revenue Recognition, then Revenue Rule Library. Default rules apply natively.
cards.example: A Monthly SaaS Subscription Rule that matches the subscription product.

cards.title: Point in time vs over time
cards.body: Point in time recognises the full amount at one moment and reveals a Trigger point field (for example invoice approval). Over time spreads revenue and reveals the distribution method dropdown.
cards.example: A one-time setup fee is point in time; a subscription is over time.

cards.title: Criteria
cards.body: Choose a column (for example Product, Pricing model, Contract item name, Product start date, Business entity), the condition (only equals) and a value. More filters combine with AND. You can also add more products to one POB.
cards.example: Pricing model equals Per unit AND Business entity equals the US entity.

cards.title: Why products need different rules
cards.body: Each product delivers service differently, so each is recognised differently: a platform fee evenly over the term, a usage product by actual usage, an implementation fee over the implementation period only.
cards.example: A $10,000 implementation fee delivered over 3 months is recognised over 3 months, not the contract term.

cards.title: POB policies
cards.body: Immediate recognises revenue as soon as the invoice is created. Deferred records the invoice amount as a liability and recognises it gradually. Unbilled covers service delivered before any invoice and applies to postpaid cases only.
cards.example: Annual prepaid subscription: Deferred. Usage billed in arrears: Unbilled.

cards.title: Equally by days
cards.body: Spreads the amount across the actual service days in each month. Monthly revenue = total value × (service days in the month ÷ total service days).
cards.example: A month with more service days recognises more.

cards.title: Equally by month
cards.body: Divides the total evenly across the months, ignoring month length.
cards.example: $12,000 over 12 months: $1,000 a month.

cards.title: Configurable days monthly
cards.body: Sets a daily baseline rate and multiplies it by the days in each billing month.
cards.example: $36,500 a year at $100 a day: $3,100 in January, $2,800 in February, $3,000 in April.

cards.title: Usage based
cards.body: Recognises revenue equal to metered consumption in each period. Needs accurate usage tracking.
cards.example: 10 active seats at $10: $100 recognised that period.

cards.title: Entitlement based
cards.body: Defers the full amount at purchase and recognises it as the upfront value is consumed, delivered or expires.
cards.example: A $120,000 prepaid credit pool recognised as credits are used, with unused credits recognised at expiry.

cards.title: Aggregate based
cards.body: Recognises in proportion to the share of total expected activity delivered. Depends on a reliable estimate of total activity.
cards.example: $120,000 contract, 12M expected syncs, 100k syncs in month 2: $1,000.

cards.title: Equally by months with estimated price
cards.body: Spreads an estimated total evenly, then corrects the difference when actuals are final, using the contract's deviation strategy.
cards.example: $12,000 estimate, $13,200 actual: $1,000 for Jan to Nov and $2,200 in December including the $1,200 true-up.

cards.title: Set up, ingest, run
cards.body: Set up the rule library, ingest the contract, performance obligations are created, then the revenue recognition job calculates each month's revenue automatically.
cards.example: No spreadsheet work at month end.

cards.title: Review, edit, transfer
cards.body: The job produces draft entries. Edit lines or add tags, then transfer. Transfer locks the period and syncs the entries to the ERP.
cards.example: Close September: run the job for Sep 30, review, transfer.

edgeCases: Separate clocks. Recognition dates are independent of invoice and payment dates.
The 5% rule. Material adjustments above 5% are front-loaded.
Closed means closed. After closing, nothing in the period can change, so always validate first.
Not legal advice. Zenskar does not assess whether a contract is legally enforceable or replace accounting judgment.
Entitlements. They are off-balance-sheet and not reconciled with financial transactions.
Version note. Accounting was reorganized in the newer docs; confirm what your tenant has enabled.
Criteria are exact. Only an equals condition is supported, and several filters combine with AND.
Priority and conflicts. The docs do not describe rule priority or what happens when two rules match the same product.
Trigger points. Only invoice approval is documented as a point-in-time trigger.
Unbilled policy. It applies to postpaid cases only.

Entitlement overdraw. If the contract allows a negative balance, overdrawn consumption is still recognised and the balance goes negative. A later true-up that replenishes the balance is deferred, not recognised.
Docs example. The Equally by days example in the docs does not reconcile (its day counts and amounts disagree); verify the day-count basis before relying on it.
Revenue equals billing. A frequent client mistake. Surface it; the client's accountant and auditor decide treatment.

quiz.question: Which method fits a usage-priced service?
An adjustment is 8% of the contract. Which method is required?
What does back-load do?
options: Defers to the final period when outcomes are certain

quiz.question: Before closing a period you should…
quiz.explanation: Validation returns a checklist without closing.

quiz.question: Does revenue follow the invoice date?
quiz.explanation: Recognition depends on performance, not billing.

quiz.question: Which condition do revenue rule criteria support?
quiz.explanation: Only exact-match equals is supported; multiple filters combine with AND.

quiz.question: A $36,500 annual contract is set to Configurable days monthly at $100 per day. What does February recognise?

qa.question: Billing vs revenue recognition?
qa.answer: Billing is what you charge and when. Revenue is when you have earned it.

qa.question: Straight-line vs usage-based vs entitlement-based distribution?
qa.answer: Straight-line spreads evenly, usage-based follows consumption, entitlement-based follows credits, milestones or features.

qa.question: Front-load vs straight-line vs back-load adjustment?
qa.answer: Front-load books the change in the next open period, straight-line spreads it over remaining periods, back-load defers it to the last period.

qa.question: Over time vs point in time?
qa.answer: Subscriptions are recognized over time; deliveries and milestones at a point in time.

qa.question: Validate vs close a period?
qa.answer: Validate returns a checklist without closing. Close locks the period.

qa.question: Journal entry vs journal line?
qa.answer: An entry groups lines that make the accounting posting.

qa.question: Balance sheet vs income statement?
qa.answer: Position at a date versus performance over a period.

qa.question: Entitlement vs recognized revenue?
qa.answer: Entitlements are usage rights, off-balance-sheet, and not reconciled to revenue.

qa.question: Annual subscription revenue?
qa.answer: Straight-line over the term.

qa.question: Metered consumption contract?
qa.answer: Usage-based distribution.

qa.question: Scope increases 10% mid-term?
qa.answer: Material (above 5%), so front-load.

qa.question: Month-end close?
qa.answer: Validate, fix gaps, then close the period.

qa.question: Milestone-based service?
qa.answer: Entitlement-based distribution.

qa.question: Material threshold?
qa.answer: Adjustments above 5% must be front-loaded.

qa.question: Can I edit a closed period?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: Is a legally unenforceable contract flagged?
qa.answer: No. Zenskar does not assess legal enforceability or replace accounting judgment.

qa.question: Does the invoice date move revenue?
qa.answer: No.

qa.question: What if usage overshoots the forecast?
qa.answer: Monitoring flags the variance and an adjustment schedule is proposed with rationale and approval.

qa.question: What are the five steps?
qa.answer: Identify the contract, identify obligations, determine the price, allocate it, recognize revenue.

qa.question: How are obligations identified?
qa.answer: From the products and features configured in each phase.

qa.question: What is kept for audit?
qa.answer: Rationale, approval workflow and an audit trail for each adjustment.

qa.question: Equally by days vs equally by month vs configurable days monthly?
qa.answer: By days weights each month by its service days, by month gives every month the same amount, and configurable days monthly applies a daily baseline rate times the days in each billing month.

qa.question: Immediate vs Deferred vs Unbilled policy?
qa.answer: Immediate recognises on invoice creation. Deferred holds the invoice as a liability and releases it over time. Unbilled is for service delivered before invoicing, postpaid only.

qa.question: Platform fee, usage product and implementation fee on one contract.
qa.answer: Three rules: the platform fee evenly over the term, the usage product by actual usage, and the implementation fee over the implementation period.

qa.question: Variable consideration with an estimate.
qa.answer: Use equally by months with estimated transaction price. When actuals are final the difference is trued up using the adjustment method.

qa.question: Two rules match the same product.
qa.answer: The docs do not describe priority or conflicts, so test it and confirm with an SME.

qa.question: Entitlement-based contract overdraws its credits.
qa.answer: Overdrawn consumption is still recognised and the balance goes negative; a later replenishing true-up is deferred.

qa.question: Where do I create a revenue rule?
qa.answer: Accounting, then Revenue Recognition, then Revenue Rule Library, then Create Revenue Rule. Fill in rule information, distribution, criteria, then save.
